f4b4bb981e:d0e1f30ecc70a48f.title: Instytut Adama Mickiewicza
f4b4bb981e:d0e1f30ecc70a48f.summary: The project, developed in collaboration with the Adam Mickiewicz Institute (IAM) team and the Culture.pl editorial team, aimed to build relationships with artists and creative communities (IAM visual identity) and present Polish culture and its creators to an international audience (Culture.pl). IAM works with artists and people in the cultural sector who think outside the box, experiment, challenge existing ideas and take risks. We wanted the Institute's visual identity to reflect this open and bold approach, while giving space to the work itself. Rather than compete with the artists' work for attention, the visual identity provides a clear, distinctive and flexible frame for presenting it.

f4b4bb981e:45a9357592e12b67.title: Where You Stand Shapes What You Can See
f4b4bb981e:45a9357592e12b67.summary: Our experiences, assumptions, and emotions influence how we see the world. The same moment can hold different meanings depending on who is looking, where they stand, and what they bring with them.

f4b4bb981e:c911b390534d0537.title: Aether Scent
f4b4bb981e:c911b390534d0537.summary: A quiet bloom of botanical resonance, unfolding across seven living species. Aether Scent is a studio exploration of nature through a digital lens. An imagined collection of botanical essences in which every specimen moves between the familiar and the unknown, retaining traces of its organic origin while growing into something new.

f4b4bb981e:cd8abe45d7552823.title: Mascot Collection
f4b4bb981e:cd8abe45d7552823.summary: Meet Flowy, Glowy, and Peanut! Three little characters with their own personalities, looks, and stories. We had fun creating this collection and exploring different emotions, poses, and ways to bring these guys into apps, social media, and branding. Hope you enjoy them as much as we do!

f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.title: Noche en Blanco Málaga 2026
f4b4bb981e:c460ad19d835a4f4.summary: LNEB es un evento dedicado a la creación cultural en Málaga, que acoge actividades, exposiciones y propuestas artísticas abiertas al público. Esta edición se desarrolla bajo el lema "El futuro se escribe con música", una temática que toma la música como punto de partida para conectar cultura, innovación y participación ciudadana. Para su identidad visual nos hemos inspirado en el movimiento y la vibración del sonido. La propuesta se construye a partir de una tipografía variable y un sistema gráfico vivo, capaz de transformarse y reaccionar a la música. Las formas circulares que componen las letras hacen referencia a los ciclos lunares, conectando visualmente con el imaginario del evento. El sistema visual se expande mediante texturas, deformaciones y animaciones influenciadas por el Op Art, utilizando colores vibrantes y contrastados que refuerzan el carácter del evento. La identidad busca convertirse en una experiencia dinámica e interactiva.

f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.title: TIDAL SCULPTURES ? Iceland
f4b4bb981e:ec58974820919c94.summary: Temporary sand islands in a lagoon on Iceland's east coast, shaped by wind, tides, and rain. Low evening light reveals sculptural ridges, dark textures, and cool blue water.

f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.title: Farseer
f4b4bb981e:a363c7135b5c591b.summary: Farseer is a financial planning platform built around a spreadsheet interface, giving finance teams a familiar environment with high-performance technology underneath. The brand was built on the same principle. Spreadsheets became the foundation of the identity system, shaped into a visual language that feels lighter, faster, and more human than traditional finance software. When a product changes the way people work, it changes the way they feel about work too. We rebuilt Farseer across verbal identity, visual identity, motion, audio, sub-brands, and a new website.

f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.title: Tiempos inciertos
f4b4bb981e:b3a821c5df2d9011.summary: Visual identity and graphic communication system for Tiempos inciertos (Uncertain Times), the international congress organised by ADACE, the Spanish Association of Contemporary Art Directors, held at the Federico García Lorca Centre in Granada. The event reflects on the present and future of cultural institutions, addressing issues such as governance, collections, sustainability, new technologies and audiences. The graphic proposal builds on ADACE's distinctive yellow underline, a recurring element of its visual identity, expanding it into a vibrant palette inspired by text highlighters. The title Tiempos inciertos is partially obscured by the bands themselves, evoking a present marked by uncertainty, in which everything seems to be under review and in search of balance.

f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.title: OTZ LAB
f4b4bb981e:61c3db0238d957c7.summary: OTZ LAB is OTEYZA's unisex fragrance collection. We designed the bottle, packaging and visual identity to translate the brand's dialogue between tradition and the avant-garde into perfumery. The bottle pairs the solidity of matte black steel with the fragility of glass, shaped like a test tube to evoke experimentation. A sphere in distinctive colours and textures identifies each fragrance, while the boxes feature compositions inspired by constructivism. A design that reinterprets traditional perfume packaging through structure, material and intention.

f4b4bb981e:0bcd3a79518fc6fb.title: Came from the stars
f4b4bb981e:0bcd3a79518fc6fb.summary: Another installment of the creative project exploring new Carpathian myths. Illustrations inspired by Hutsul folklore and Carpathian cultural aesthetics.

f4b4bb981e:e51d7a75dde3cf12.title: Shania Twain for the Sunday Times

f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.title: Piega
f4b4bb981e:8ff2934edd02d3de.summary: PIEGA is a brand direction for a women's label built on the fold. The symbol is a paper pentagon folded into seven pieces. The logo prints itself in reverse, the way wet ink does when you fold a page. Every garment keeps a red the street never sees: a lining, a hem tape, the back of a fold.

f4b4bb981e:7de9560f4ddf0c63.title: Our very first painting exhibition
f4b4bb981e:7de9560f4ddf0c63.summary: This exhibition explores the meaning of space and place through personal experiences and memories. Each individual shapes their own environment over time, turning it into more than just a physical setting. Everyday moments, like sitting on a chair or drinking water, become part of a deeper emotional landscape.

f4b4bb981e:bdad977510edfa7e.title: Quantum Security Brand Identity & Pitch Deck
f4b4bb981e:bdad977510edfa7e.summary: Quantum Deep is a deep-tech company building probabilistic computing hardware for cybersecurity, semiconductors, and post-quantum cryptography. Ahead of a new funding round, they came to us for a brand identity mature enough to match their technology and win the confidence of investors and enterprise customers. We built the full brand foundation: strategy, tone of voice, and a complete visual system with logo, typography, and color. Rather than leaning on generic quantum clichés, we designed a graphic language rooted in probability, photonics, and structured uncertainty. It scales across every touchpoint, from the website and investor pitch decks to 3D product visualization of the chip, brand guidelines, social, and events. A credible, category-defining identity for a B2B deep-tech brand, by Prznt Perfect.

f4b4bb981e:b376d07938fdff15.title: Portraits 2023-2026
f4b4bb981e:b376d07938fdff15.summary: A collection of hand-drawn digital portrait illustrations inspired by classical engraving, woodcut and traditional pen and ink techniques. The portraits were created for a variety of commercial and editorial projects, including advertising campaigns, corporate portraits, brand identity, packaging design, and commissioned artwork. Combining detailed linework, crosshatching, and a monochrome palette, these illustrations reinterpret the visual language of historical engraving in a contemporary digital medium.

f4b4bb981e:840a78a91f95502a.summary: Da San Chaek Gil is a brand representing the commercial and cultural district of Dasan New Town in Namyangju. Supported by the city government and the Regional Intellectual Property Center under the Korean Intellectual Property Office, FRONT KIT conducted its total branding including the naming which indicates "Da San (area) + San Chaek (stroll) + Chaek (book) + Gil (path)," that are the features of the district. Also, the project encompassed the creation of a comprehensive brand identity, including slogans, storytelling, characters, and application designs that reflect Dasan's vibrant scenery and cultural sentiment. Additionally, intellectual property rights were filed, workshops for merchants were conducted, and the geographic name was officially registered, ensuring a systematic and professional public branding. a4977d3fa4:e2c908a14a76e111.title: Issy Wood Intimate ‘Self-Portraits’ Rock National Portrait Gallery in London
a4977d3fa4:e2c908a14a76e111.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:e2c908a14a76e111.summary: Summary American-born, British-raised artist and musician has unveiled a new solo, 'Self-Portraits,' at London's National Portrait GalleryOn through February 2027, the exhibition launches the Gallery's new Artist Focus program, dedicated to talents pushing portraiture into new territories Even in a visual world steeped in digital circulation, a hunger for figurative painting persists. Issy Wood is a British-American artist and musician who has have lifted the profile of a new generation of painters braiding classical and conceptual technique with the strange textures of youth culture today.Hot off a major exhibition at the Kistefos Museum in Norway, the artist heads home to London for a spotlight at none other than the National Portrait Gallery for her first solo of self-portraits. Wood is the inaugural Artist Focus featuree, a new platform at the Gallery dedicated to voices shaking up the sub-genre, and the show comprises 12 works, seven of which making their public debut.Wood came to the self-portraits through “a very practical urge” to supply stand-in visuals when a magazine “[threatened] to send a photographer over to my studio,” she explained in a recent interview. She began the series in 2020 and has also lent her brush to the stars; last year, she completed a dreamy cover of Charli xcx, who owns several of Wood’s works, for Vanity Fair’s first art issue in nearly 20 years.Through Wood’s image in Self-Portraits emerges threads of intimacy, consumer culture, and the complexity of identity, reveling in fragmentation as the truest form of self-representation. The personal is not embodied by what is revealed, but what is obscured, masked, and distorted. View this post on InstagramA post shared by HypeArt (@hypeart) Issy Wood: Self-Portraits is now on view through February 28, 2027.National Portrait GallerySt. Martin's Pl,London WC2H 0HE,United Kingdom Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:3133ce9ad27c3352.title: Westwing Brings Victoria Beckham’s Signature Style to the Dinner Table
a4977d3fa4:3133ce9ad27c3352.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:3133ce9ad27c3352.summary: After opening its online shop in the UK earlier this year, Westwing, the European home and living brand, now teams up with British designer Victoria Beckham on an exclusive dining collection. Marking her debut in the home and interiors, the landmark collaboration leans into the designer’s background in fashion and beauty through the theme “Serving Style.” It aims to translate Victoria Beckham’s famously refined aesthetic from her eponymous fashion label into a line of elegant tableware, textiles and decorative pieces that turn everyday gatherings into elevated experiences around the table. “Home is where some of life's most meaningful moments happen,” shared Victoria Beckham in an official statement. “This collaboration felt like a natural way to explore that world through the same lens of design, craftsmanship and attention to detail that defines everything we do as a brand.”From chain-patterned plate sets to carved cutlery reminiscent of flowing dresses, the dining collection draws elements from her signature pieces to create synergy between the catwalk and the home. Similarly, a clean color palette builds on this connection with white, silver, and notes of green tying the assortment together. Elsewhere, metal-crafted products in the range, including napkin holders, shell-shaped dishes and serving spoons, adopt a hammered finish inspired by the 19th-century Arts and Crafts movement. Complementing their textured surfaces, vases and glassware feature soft ripple-like edges to round off the line with a subtle yet sleek style.Reflecting on the collaboration, CEO of Westwing Andreas Hoerning said, “Partnering with Victoria Beckham is a defining moment for Westwing. Her unmistakable aesthetic has shaped contemporary fashion for years, and we are proud to bring that same vision into the world of Beautiful Living. This Collection creates a natural dialogue between fashion and interiors, offering Design Lovers a new way to express their personal style at home.”In a new…

a4977d3fa4:f42130145d0b3fa8.title: Alfa Romeo Unveils Radical Cuorerosso Concept During the Paris Motor Show
a4977d3fa4:f42130145d0b3fa8.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f42130145d0b3fa8.summary: Summary Alfa Romeo unveiled the Cuorerosso concept vehicle during Paris Motor ShowA special edition of the 33 Stradale was also unveiled, which pays homage to Paris, FranceAlfa Romeo used the exhibit to roadmap its design language and powertrain plans for the future For this year's Paris Motor Show, Alfa Romeo brought out a selection of gorgeous vehicles, both of which exemplify why many enthusiasts and industry leaders say the Italian brand is the heart and soul of automotive.Alfa Romeo took the opportunity at this year's Paris Motor Show to unveil a brand new concept, called the Cuorerosso. The world-premiere concept befittingly translates to "Red Heart" and is positioned not as a preview of a production model, but as a manifesto for where the company is headed next. Its design is shaped under a “Necessary Beauty” design philosophy; the 4700 mm-long 2+2 coupé was sculpted like a single block of material, resulting in a monolithic, liquid-metal silhouette that crosses between grand tourer and supercar. The Cuorerosso is filled with heritage cues: a wedge line running into a Coda Tronca tail, a Scudetto-shaped rear window, rear-hinged back doors and forged wheels riffing on the classic “telephone dial” design. Inside, a reworked “Cannocchiale Vivente” cluster pared back information as driving grew more intense, while Poltrona Frau nubuck, recycled carbon fiber and a lightweight fabric borrowed from Luna Rossa’s sailing gear rounded out the cabin. Alfa said the concept previewed a multi-energy future topped by a 2.9-liter V6 full-hybrid with Q4 all-wheel drive, all finished in a shape-shifting Liquid Ink Red that read anywhere from vibrant crimson to near-black depending on the light.Sharing the stand was Alfa's coachbuilt 33 Stradale halo car, this time dressed for the occasion in a one-off tribute to the French capital. Tone-on-tone gloss and matte damask graphics stood alongside an oversized Quadrifoglio insignia, nodding to the shared silk-weaving heritage of…

a4977d3fa4:8000843bc58b01f0.title: Les Benjamins & Apple Go "From Earth to Sky" in Turkey Runway Show
a4977d3fa4:8000843bc58b01f0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:8000843bc58b01f0.summary: SummaryLes Benjamins partnered with Apple for its 15th-anniversary "From Earth to Sky" collection in Cappadocia, blending East and West.The runway show, featuring custom hot-air balloons, was designed on iPad Pro and filmed on iPhone 18 Pro Max.On Wednesday, Les Bejamins teamed up with Apple to bring its new collection to life, showcasing the “From Earth to Sky” spectacle in Cappadocia, Turkey. Shot on the iPhone 18 Pro Max by French filmmaker Neels Castillon, Bünyamin Aydın’s latest show celebrated 15 years of his Istanbul-based lifestyle brand.Inspired by his Anatolian heritage, Aydın began developing the collection in early 2026 with the iPad Pro (with Apple Pencil Pro) and iPhone 17 Pro Max, capturing photos and 4K video for inspiration, assembling moodboards on Freeform and prototyping the custom-built hot-air balloons on Procreate. On working with the Apple Pencil and iPad, the designer explained, “Working with regular pen and paper feels very natural, but the hover feature on Apple Pencil Pro lets me preview every stroke before I even make it, so I can see any mistakes beforehand.”The collection itself represents Aydın’s multicultural heritage, having been born in Germany. With what he calls a “German discipline and Turkish heart,” the duality runs through the collection. “The canvas is the West; the paint is the East,” Aydın shared about the collection, which combines contemporary silhouettes with Turkish fabrics, along with Silk Road influences. Even the massive hot air balloons drew from the flora of the Anatolian landscape, depicting green Echinops, pink trumpets, and yellow tulips. “I see my role as that of a translator and a bridge between East and West,” Aydın added. “I hope this project makes Turkish people proud.”To capture the runway show, Castillon utilized the iPhone 18 Pro Max’s variable aperture to achieve smooth transitions while filming in varied sunlight, leaning on the A20 Pro chip to sustain continuous 4K recording without overheating. By…

a4977d3fa4:be40743ea74730cc.title: MING and Massena LAB Rework Their Honey Collaboration Five Years Later
a4977d3fa4:be40743ea74730cc.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:be40743ea74730cc.summary: Summary MING and Massena LAB reunite for the 57.09 Secret Honey.Three rotating sapphire discs create a constantly shifting “dynamic guilloché” display.Limited to 125 pieces, it pairs tri-tone titanium lugs with a 50-hour automatic movement. MING and Massena LAB” are revisiting one of their earliest collaborations with the new 57.09 Secret Honey, a far more elaborate sequel to 2021’s 17.09 Honey and 17.09 Black.Five years after the original 200-piece collaboration introduced a vintage-inspired honeycomb motif, the two independent names — now fellow members of the Alternative Horological Alliance — have combined both earlier palettes into a single watch. Rather than reproducing the honeycomb literally, the 57.09 transforms the idea into what MING calls “dynamic guilloché,” using three rotating sapphire discs above a dark brown lacquered base dial to create a constantly changing interference pattern. The warm honey tone appears only as the discs move and overlap, giving the “Secret Honey” name a literal role in the design.Each sapphire disc rotates at a different rate - once every 24 hours, 12 hours and 60 minutes - with individual aperture patterns and luminous treatments in orange-emitting Super-LumiNova and MING Polar White. The 12-hour and 60-minute discs also carry the honey-colored hour and minute indications, while the indices and MING and Massena LAB logos are engraved into the box-style sapphire crystal above, creating a second luminous layer after dark.Surrounding the display is a 40mm Grade 5 titanium case using MING’s fifth-generation architecture, distinguished here by triple-stepped, tri-tone lugs assembled from nine individual components. Natural titanium forms the outer step, yellow-gold-referencing TiN coats the middle section and rose-gold-toned TiSiN finishes the innermost layer, visually extending the dial’s shifting black-and-honey palette into the case itself.Powering the watch is the automatic Sellita for MING 330.M2, running at 4 Hz and…

a4977d3fa4:7752991019c832ce.title: Seeing Red in Milan: Inside The 50 Best Bars 2026
a4977d3fa4:7752991019c832ce.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:7752991019c832ce.summary: In the world of mixology, the clearest sign that you’ve made it is a red ceremonial scarf, handed to every team that lands on The 50 Best Bars list. On October 7, that scarf made its last appearance of the year in Milan, where the global edition of The 50 Best Bars 2026 brought the international cocktail community to the city for the first time.The ceremony took over the Palazzo del Ghiaccio, a Liberty-style landmark that opened in 1923 as Europe’s largest indoor ice rink and now hosts runway shows and gala nights. For one evening, the city that gave the world aperitivo culture became the center of it. Bartenders, bar owners and brands from 26 cities arrived via the red carpet for a drinks reception before the night’s main event.Milan marked the final stop on a long road for Cointreau, which spent 2026 as the official sponsor of the iconic red scarf ceremony across all four of The 50 Best Bars 2026 ceremonies. That run took the scarf from North America to Asia and, for the very first time, to Europe. It was the brand’s second year as Official Orange Liqueur Partner, and it came with a promise of bigger, bolder moments at every stop under the “Shake It Up” banner. For a brand that has spent more than a century and a half inside some of the world’s most enduring cocktails, from the Margarita to the Sidecar and the Cosmopolitan, the tagline doubled as a statement of intent.Cointreau Spicy, the brand’s chili-infused spin on its signature orange liqueur, carried that promise into the glass all season, with appearances in Vancouver and Amsterdam, where it starred in a Spicy Watermelon Margarita at the inaugural The 50 Best Bars Europe edition. In Milan, the Cointreau booth closed out the year with cocktails featuring both Cointreau L’Unique and Cointreau Spicy, including two standout serves created by the team at Lyaness: the Cointreau Bubbles, a vibrant celebration of orange in all its complexity, and the Spiced Carrot Margarita, a bold twist on the classic cocktail…

a4977d3fa4:d936ac185cf6f2f4.title: BEAMS Stitches Three Leathers Into One Broken-In Blouson
a4977d3fa4:d936ac185cf6f2f4.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:d936ac185cf6f2f4.summary: Summary BEAMS’ new Leather Blouson combines sheep nappa, sheep nubuck and goat suede in a paneled constructionWashing, tumbling and hand-applied distressing give each jacket a worn-for-years look straight off the rackThe design draws on vintage sports jackets, reworked with a wide body and shortened length BEAMS has introduced the Leather Blouson as part of its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, a jacket built from three contrasting leathers and finished to look like a long-owned favorite. Offered in Soft Black and Taupe, the piece pairs a vintage sports jacket template with a contemporary wide, cropped silhouette.The jacket’s character starts with its materials, as BEAMS splices together three distinct hides across the body. Smooth sheep nappa and velvety sheep nubuck sit alongside goat suede, with the varying textures set against one another through bold paneling rather than blended into a single surface.Each jacket then goes through a multi-step aging process designed to replicate years of wear. Washing and tumbling break down the leather and draw out a faded tone, after which every piece is individually worked by hand to add the scuffs and highlights that typically form at stress points over time. Because the distressing is done one jacket at a time, the placement and intensity of the wear vary from piece to piece, along with the natural creases and color shifts inherent to the leather itself.Structurally, the blouson takes its cues from vintage sports jackets, updated with practical touches for daily use. Hand-warmer pockets sit at the front, each concealing a zippered security pocket inside, while ribbed trims finish the shape and a polyester lining keeps the interior smooth.BEAMS cuts the jacket in what it calls a Wide Short Fit, pairing a roomy chest with a deliberately shortened length. The boxy proportions give the piece a classic yet updated outline that works well over hoodies and heavier knits for layered looks.The BEAMS Leather Blouson is available now in…

a4977d3fa4:695e58aedd11d900.title: Apple’s HomePod mini 2 Just Joined Your Home Theater
a4977d3fa4:695e58aedd11d900.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:695e58aedd11d900.summary: Summary Apple’s HomePod mini 2 pairs the S10 chip with computational audio that tunes playback to each track in real timeA new Sound Glow feature turns the speaker’s top into a reactive light canvas synced to bass, treble and album artThe speaker arrives in pink, green, blue, white and midnight, with Siri AI landing in a future software update Apple has unveiled HomePod mini 2, the second generation of its pocket-sized smart speaker, rebuilt around the S10 chip and a fresh five-color lineup. The update brings Sound Glow, a reactive lighting layer across the top surface, along with support for four-speaker surround sound, Mac speaker duty and the overhauled Siri AI assistant, which is set to arrive through a later software update.At the core of the speaker is the Apple S10 chip, which drives a computational audio system that reads music as it plays and adjusts dynamic range, loudness and acoustic output on the fly. The result is 360-degree sound from the same compact footprint, scalable from a single unit to a stereo pair or a full multiroom configuration.Sound Glow is the most visible addition, transforming the speaker’s top into a lit surface that pulses and shifts in real time with the low and high frequencies of a track. Colors are pulled from the album artwork in Now Playing, so each song generates its own palette, while ambient soundscapes such as rain trigger custom animations designed for winding down. Controlling Sound Glow by voice requires an Apple Intelligence-enabled iPhone.Those lighting effects play off the new finishes, offered in pink, green, blue, white and midnight and designed to coordinate with Apple’s Mac colorways. HomePod mini 2 can now act as the audio output for any Mac with Wi-Fi 6E or later, either solo or as a stereo pair, covering movies, games and video calls. “HomePod mini 2 brings together Siri AI, gorgeous new colors, and incredible audio,” said Kaiann Drance, Apple’s vice president of Worldwide Home Product Marketing, in a press…

According to a new report from GamesBeat citing sources familiar with the matter, Rockstar Games is slated to drop the PC version of the blockbuster title in the first quarter of 2027. If the timeline holds, PC players could be running the game by the end of March 2027. a4977d3fa4:9113877ad13c7707.title: The Zaha Hadid Foundation Converts Its Historic London Headquarters Into a Public Cultural Hub
a4977d3fa4:9113877ad13c7707.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:9113877ad13c7707.summary: Summary Zaha Hadid Foundation is opening Hadid’s former London headquarters as a public cultural space.The restored building preserves key Hadid-designed details.Opening November 3, it will host exhibitions, talks, workshops and archival programs. Ten years after Zaha Hadid’s passing, the Zaha Hadid Foundation is opening the architect’s former London headquarters to the public as a new cultural space dedicated to architecture, design and the related arts. Located at 10 Bowling Green Lane in Clerkenwell, the Grade II-listed Victorian schoolhouse served as Hadid’s practice for more than three decades before being reworked by London studio KA, led by Katherine Nolan and Alex Butterworth.The refurbishment draws together its different histories: original fireplaces and previously closed doorways have been restored, while Hadid-designed details - including Z-shaped door pulls and shard-like flooring insets - remain intact. New finishes reference colors found in her paintings, while the reconfigured ground floor introduces galleries, a learning space, lecture hall and collection displays alongside furniture and objects from Zaha Hadid Design.Opening to the public on November 3, the space will position Hadid’s extensive archive not simply as a record of her career, but as a starting point for exhibitions, talks, workshops, residencies and conversations with contemporary practitioners. Its inaugural exhibition, Zaha Hadid: Architecture of Performance, curated by Catherine Howe and Libby Sellers, explores the architect’s lesser-seen involvement with performance and stage design, spanning her 1989 collaboration with choreographer Rosemary Butcher, designs for the Pet Shop Boys’ Nightlife World Tour and her 2014 staging of Mozart’s “Così fan tutte.” Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:8b871d9228131762.summary: Summary Ben Affleck confirmed that Lucasfilm offered him the directing job on 'Star Wars: The Force Awakens'before he turned it downThe 2015 sequel went on to be helmed by JJ Abrams and generated over $2 billion USD at the worldwide box officeAffleck explained that he stepped away because someone with greater passion would do a better job navigating the franchise and its vocal fanbase Lucasfilm previously offered Ben Affleck the chance to helm Star Wars: The Force Awakens before the 2015 sci-fi sequel went on to gross over $2 billion USD worldwide. The filmmaker reflected on the missed blockbuster during an appearance on the Happy Sad Confused podcast while promoting his political thriller Animals.Reflecting on his career behind the camera, Affleck noted that passing on high-profile projects has rarely caused him regret. "There haven't been too many movies that I turned down, whether as an actor or a director that I thought, 'That was a shame,'" he explained. Though a fan of the franchise, Affleck realized the immense responsibility of reviving the property required a different perspective. a4977d3fa4:60cf78e43e84d66f.title: Kith Digs Into the Armani Archives for “Dreams of the Dune” FW26

a4977d3fa4:60cf78e43e84d66f.summary: SummaryThe FW26 “Dreams of the Dune” collection blends Armani’s vintage tailoring with Kith’s modern streetwear, featuring neutral tones and collaborations with ASICS, Diemme, and ’47.Launching globally on October 16, the range will be available online and at select Kith and Armani stores.For their third collaborative collection, Kith and Giorgio Armani took to the Moroccan desert for an outdoor runway show inspired by one of Ronnie Fieg’s favorite periods of the Italian brand. Looking to Armani’s desert-inspired Sahara collections and campaigns from the late ‘80s and early ‘90s, the two labels created a range that traverses both Kith’s contemporary streetwear roots and Armani’s European sartorial traditions.Referencing archival seasons like Fall/Winter 1990 and Spring/Summer 1992, the latest collection was interlaced with Armani signatures — relaxed tailoring juxtaposed with fluid fabrics and leather outerwear. In keeping with a dry, desert palette, color was largely neutral throughout, ranging from black, navy, tan, gray, brown, and white. Modern twists were provided by Ronnie Fieg’s streetwear touch, along with collaborative pieces with ASICS, Diemme, and ’47. The final result is layered, not only in the historical sense, but in its physical manifestation: coats worn over pullovers with turtlenecks underneath, and elsewhere, a shirt and necktie with a leather jacket and a padded trench coat. There were also unexpected moments of layering, counterbalancing the range’s tailored feel, including printed compression pants worn with shorts, scarves around the hip, and neck gaiters covering the face. New accessories like the ASICS GEL-MAI 0.1 in “Quarry” and “Safari,” along with the range of ‘47 Yankees caps, stood out against the collection’s tailored silhouettes and luxurious materials like suede, silk, virgin wool, cashmere, and pure hemp. Far from excessive, these juxtapositions between the everyday and the formal, the past and the present, and ultimately, Fieg…

a4977d3fa4:262b0e7bf5b24c25.title: Hublot Levels Up Modern Luxury Horology with Patrick Mahomes and the Big Bang Reloaded Collection
a4977d3fa4:262b0e7bf5b24c25.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:262b0e7bf5b24c25.summary: Luxury watchmaking and professional football might seem like fundamentally different worlds, but Hublot found a natural fit when it brought star quarterback Patrick Mahomes on board as a brand ambassador in late 2025. The partnership pairs a three-time champion known for shattering records with a Swiss watchmaker defined by its willingness to challenge conventional standards. Both share an obsession with peak performance, split-second precision, and pushing past traditional limits.Building on that momentum, Hublot kicked off spring 2026 in Geneva by rolling out the Big Bang Reloaded collection. Marking two decades of the iconic Big Bang lineup and 16 years of its proprietary Unico movement, the release re-engineers the open-worked chronograph from the inside out. The collection reflects Hublot’s transition into a fully realized Manufacture where in-house calibers drive the entire lineup.At the center of the mechanical redesign is the HUB1280 UNICO caliber, a 354-component flyback chronograph packed with five distinct patented innovations. Visual enhancements make the inner mechanics far more striking, highlighting a color-accented column wheel at 6 o'clock and a dual oscillating clutch at 8 o'clock through the skeleton dial. Practically speaking, it offers a robust 72-hour power reserve and water resistance up to 100 meters, ensuring elite-level performance off the field.The collection showcases Hublot’s material mastery across five key references, honoring milestone anniversaries like 20 years of the All Black concept and 15 years of Magic Gold. Highlighted by Mahomes, the Magic Gold edition pairs a polished 18K Magic Gold case—a proprietary material developed with EPFL that stands as the world's first scratch-resistant 18K gold—with a black-plated titanium bezel. Additional models offer full-color high-tech ceramics in blue, dark green, and all-black, alongside a lightweight titanium and ceramic hybrid.Every 44 mm timepiece features Hublot’s patented One-Click…

a4977d3fa4:f01e3fd3ad8b4dc0.title: Even Realities’ Dystopian Sculptures Are Keeping a Watchful Eye on You
a4977d3fa4:f01e3fd3ad8b4dc0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:f01e3fd3ad8b4dc0.summary: Technology company Even Realities has launched new sculptures around central London as part of its latest installation, “The Watchers.” Revealing the chilling reality of camera glasses, the installation takes shape with CCTV-mounted heads featuring camera lenses. Despite being in the tech space, Even Realities has crafted digital glasses without cameras to fit naturally into human life without interfering with others in public. Its work has long been supported by ongoing data and medical professionals, so when new research from Focaldata came to light, stating that 81% of British people would support a ban on camera glasses, it delved deeper into the rising threats of the popular product.In an open letter calling for tighter control of smart glasses, Founder and CEO Will Wang shared, “Smart glasses don’t need cameras now. While there are benefits in how they enable devices to collate visual context, the privacy trade-offs, for both the user and those around them, mean cameras should never have progressed past the blueprint without proper guardrails.”Enhancing public awareness of camera glasses, "The Watchers" installation has been fitted on Berwick Street in London’s busy Soho area. Designed in collaboration with creative production studio The Robin Collective and special effects artist Will Harvey, each sculpture is made with 3D scanning, printing and live silicone castings for a hyper-realistic yet noticeably shocking appearance.To continue highlighting the dangers of intrusive filming, the company releases a short film showcasing the sculptures in everyday locations like pubs and gyms. The video illustrates how camera glasses leave no public space untouched, advocating for long-term regulatory measures.You can now watch the film in the gallery above. To find out more about the project, read the open letter online now. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:4f12a2d39b611856.title: Le Labo Expands Its Classic Candle Line With PAPYRUS 20
a4977d3fa4:4f12a2d39b611856.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:4f12a2d39b611856.summary: Summary Le Labo unveils PAPYRUS 20, a Classic Candle honoring the ancient art of recording stories.Earthy cypriol and deep musk ground ephemeral ylang-ylang and warm labdanum.Hand-poured in a clear glass jar with Le Labo's iconic typewriter label. Le Labo turns the act of remembering into scent with PAPYRUS 20, the newest addition to its Classic Candle collection. Inspired by ancient civilizations pressing papyrus reeds into sheets capable of carrying stories across centuries, the fragrance explores a more elusive kind of preservation: memories that return through scent without warning.At its core is cypriol, a material historically associated with papyrus, bringing an earthy, dry and slightly root-like depth that feels almost like aged paper, soil and weathered wood. Against it, ylang-ylang introduces a fleeting floral softness, while warm labdanum lends an ambered, resinous glow and a musk accord settles into the background.The composition moves between something archival and something intangible — the imagined smell of an old manuscript warmed by sunlight, its pages carrying traces of earth and resin before the fragrance slowly dissolves back into the room. Le Labo describes PAPYRUS 20 as an ode to both what endures and what cannot be held, treating fragrance itself as an “archivist of the ephemeral.”Its presentation remains deliberately stripped back, allowing that tension between permanence and impermanence to continue visually. Priced at $92 USD, the 245-gram candle is hand-crafted in the U.S. using a high concentration of fragrance oils, a custom wax blend and natural-fiber wicks, housed in Le Labo’s familiar clear glass vessel with an apothecary-style personalized label. The accompanying kraft box repeats the same utilitarian typography and workshop-minded simplicity, giving the object the feeling of something catalogued, dated and stored away — almost like an archival specimen waiting to be rediscovered. For more details, head over to Le Labo’s online and…

a4977d3fa4:1739ec9ae7a557f0.title: Wrangler and ROA Reimagine Denim Workwear for FW26
a4977d3fa4:1739ec9ae7a557f0.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)

Wrangler and ROA are returning for a second collaboration for Fall/Winter 2026, continuing their exploration of the intersection between American denim heritage and Italian technical design. Building on their debut collection, the latest release revisits Wrangler's workwear roots through ROA's outdoor-oriented perspective, presenting a concise lineup designed around utility, durability and everyday versatility.The three-piece capsule comprises the Wrangler x ROA Denim Cargo, Denim Hooded Jacket and Denim 6 Panel Cap, each offered in two washes: Owl Dark and Owl Light. Together, the pieces establish a cohesive denim wardrobe that draws on traditional workwear while reflecting ROA's functional design sensibilities, with the contrasting washes offering different interpretations of the same utilitarian aesthetic.The collection's accompanying narrative takes inspiration from Edvin, a 26-year-old forestry teacher from Orsa, a small town in northern Sweden, as he prepares for a professional lumberjack championship. Rather than focusing on the competition itself, the story turns its attention to the discipline and routines that precede it, from training in the woods and maintaining equipment to sharpening axes, traveling and recovering between sessions.Through this perspective, the collaboration places the everyday realities of physical work and preparation at the center of its visual identity, reinforcing the relationship between purposeful clothing and the environments in which it is worn. The second Wrangler x ROA collection launches on October 13, 2026, and will be available online through ROA's official website and Wrangler.com. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:a24a43025ed4578d.title: The 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback Debuts With Custom Look
a4977d3fa4:a24a43025ed4578d.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:a24a43025ed4578d.summary: Summary Jeep drops the 2027 Wrangler Switchback, closing out its monthly "Twelve 4 Twelve" special edition campaignThe factory-built custom aesthetic features swapped doors and hoods in Gloss Black and Sting-Gray colorwaysOrders open in November with prices starting at $66,695 USD for the two-door Rubicon X-based configuration Jeep officially pulled the cover off the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback, serving as the twelfth and final model in its yearlong special edition rollout. Closing out the brand's ambitious "Twelve 4 Twelve" campaign, which dropped one unique Wrangler iteration every month for an entire year, the Wrangler Switchback arrives with a heavy nod to custom off-road culture. The factory-produced contrasting colorway emulates a raw, aggressive look seen on owner-modified Wranglers. By leaning into an aesthetic where mismatched body panels are historically added to achieve a custom multicolored look or replace pieces damaged during off-roading, Jeep transforms a garage-repair necessity into a factory-backed statement piece.To achieve these contrasting color schemes on the factory floor, Jeep altered its standard manufacturing rhythm. The brand sequenced Gloss Black and Sting-Gray Wranglers to run sequentially down the assembly line. Line workers manually swapped the doors of consecutively sequenced vehicles during the production cycle. Factory workers later switched the hoods during the final upfitting process. This manufacturing sequence results in two distinct mismatched exterior configurations. One configuration features gray bodywork, contrasting black doors and a matching black hood. The second option flips that color scheme, producing Wranglers with black bodywork, contrasting gray doors and a gray hood.Beyond the panel swaps, the Wrangler Switchback features vibrant Gecko accents across its exterior. Bright hits of color appear on the front grille, exterior wheel rings, bold hood graphic and rear swing-gate decal. That attention to detail extends…

a4977d3fa4:95e6e8cc48580939.summary: Summary Apple captured a record 22% of the global smartphone market in the third quarter of 2026Worldwide smartphone shipments plummeted 20% year-over-year to hit a 14-year lowAn ongoing memory crisis and rising device prices forced brands to prioritize profit over sheer volume Apple just carved out its largest third-quarter slice of the global smartphone market in history, defying a brutal industry-wide slump. According to a newly released report from Counterpoint Research, worldwide smartphone shipments plummeted 20% year-over-year during the third quarter of 2026. The severe double-digit drop pushed global shipments down to their absolute lowest third-quarter level in 14 years. While the report attributed the market decline to memory constraints and rising prices, it notably did not specify what that 20% decline translated to in absolute shipment numbers.Despite the broader market slump, Apple managed to elevate its global smartphone shipment share past the 20% threshold for the very first time in any third quarter. The tech heavyweight ultimately shipped 22% of all smartphones during Q3 2026, marking a significant jump from the 18% share it held in Q3 2025. This record-setting share came even as the brand navigated its own volume declines, largely driven by the absence of a base iPhone 18 model. Without that entry-level flagship, Apple experienced a smaller launch-month channel fill compared to what the full iPhone 17 lineup achieved a year earlier. To offset that higher shipment decline, the company leaned heavily on sustained market momentum from the older iPhone 17 series. Top-tier iPhone 18 Pro models logged a stronger launch than their direct predecessors, generating particularly heavy traction across China and India.Apple's historic surge rapidly closed the gap on Samsung, though the South Korean brand managed to maintain its first-place position in the global smartphone market with a 23% share. a4977d3fa4:098acb41b949fee3.title: James Fuentes Gallery Revisits Teruko Yokoi’s Transpacific Abstraction
a4977d3fa4:098acb41b949fee3.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:098acb41b949fee3.summary: Summary Teruko Yokoi’s A Pacific Line marks her first Los Angeles solo show in over four decades.The exhibition traces her evolution from figuration to abstraction.Works span 1954–2005, bridging Japanese aesthetics and postwar Western modernism. Teruko Yokoi’s decades-spanning practice returns to Los Angeles with A Pacific Line, a new exhibition at James Fuentes Gallery tracing the Japanese-Swiss painter’s singular path through postwar abstraction. Marking her first solo presentation in the city in more than four decades, the show carries particular resonance on the West Coast: Yokoi first arrived in the United States by ship in 1954, shortly after the end of the U.S. occupation of Japan, before enrolling at the California School of Fine Arts in San Francisco. That self-directed move became the starting point for a career shaped by continual relocation across Japan, the United States, France and Switzerland, while resisting easy placement within any single school or movement. Bringing together works made between 1954 and 2005, A Pacific Line presents Yokoi’s practice as an ongoing conversation between traditional Japanese aesthetics and postwar Western modernism.Yokoi’s early years in the U.S. marked a decisive shift from figuration toward the highly personal abstraction that would come to define her work. "Pose" from 1954 still retains the contours of a seated human figure, but its body already begins to dissolve into blocks of orange, gray and brown, anticipating her increasingly rhythmic treatment of form and color.After moving to New York in 1955, she studied with Hans Hofmann, attended the Art Students League and moved within circles that included Joan Mitchell, Kenzo Okada and Mark Rothko, while living for a period at the Chelsea Hotel with painter Sam Francis. Yet her work remained distinct from the dominant language of Abstract Expressionism. Paintings such as 1960’s "Shizen–Natur," with its deep green field, saturated blue forms and streaks of red and…

a4977d3fa4:aa17196c5b5807b8.summary: Summary Netflix has released the first trailer for director Peter Berg’s WWII feature film 'The Mosquito Bowl'Based on Buzz Bissinger’s book the narrative follows four star college athletes who enlist in the Marines following Pearl HarborThe movie opens in select theaters on October 30, 2026 ahead of its Netflix streaming debut on November 25, 2026 Netflix has officially debuted the first trailer for director Peter Berg's World War II drama, The Mosquito Bowl. The feature adapts Pulitzer Prize winner Buzz Bissinger’s bestselling book The Mosquito Bowl: A Game of Life and Death in World War II.The film stars Nicholas Galitzine as John McLaughry, Bill Skarsgård as Bob Bauman, Ray Nicholson as Tony Butkovich, and Tom Francis as Dave Schreiner. Depicting four prominent college football athletes who trade their stadium jerseys for United States Marine Corps uniforms following the attack on Pearl Harbor, the story follows their transition from collegiate sports to military combat in the Pacific theater.Berg, who also appears on screen as General Simon Buckner, constructed practical battle environments to capture the visceral realities of war. Although named after a historic football matchup between military all-stars on Guadalcanal, the production emphasizes the broader combat experience over sports action, framing the narrative as a war story centered on athletes confronting extreme circumstances.The Mosquito Bowl opens in select theaters on October 30, 2026, before arriving on Netflix on November 25, 2026. Read more at Hypebeast

a4977d3fa4:6f5a21cc865a1419.title: The Rarest Thing at Regal’s ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Screenings Might Be This Doctor Doom ‘Magic: The Gathering’ Card
a4977d3fa4:6f5a21cc865a1419.author: info@hypebeast.com (Hypebeast)
a4977d3fa4:6f5a21cc865a1419.summary: Summary Moviegoers catching Avengers: Doomsday during its opening weekend can score a promo-only version of Magic: The Gathering’s Doctor Doom, King of Latveria cardThe alternate-art piece, illustrated by Jorge Molina, depicts Doom in his signature green hood and metal mask with three masked Latverian Witches at his backSupplies are limited and the total print count has not been disclosed, making the card an early collector’s target tied to Marvel’s biggest villain Magic: The Gathering is marking the arrival of Avengers: Doomsday with an exclusive alternate-art version of its Doctor Doom, King of Latveria card, handed out to eligible fans during the film’s opening weekend. The promo pairs a fresh illustration of Marvel’s iron-masked tyrant with the same in-game abilities as the standard printing, turning a trip to the theater into a collectible drop.Artist Jorge Molina handles the new illustration, portraying Doom in full regalia with his green hood drawn and his metal faceplate locked in place. Behind him stand three Latverian Witches, their faces hidden behind masks of their own, framing the image as a portrait of a ruler and his court rather than a straightforward action shot.Beneath the art, the card plays exactly like the original. Doctor Doom, King of Latveria first appeared in the Doom Prevails Commander deck within Magic’s Marvel Super Heroes collection, where he causes opponents to lose life when land cards are discarded and powers up other Villain creatures on the battlefield. That makes the promo a cosmetic upgrade for existing Doom players and a standalone chase piece for collectors who care more about the artwork than the deck.Regal revealed the giveaway during New York Comic Con, tying it specifically to its Infinity Vision premium format. To qualify, fans need to be members of the theater chain’s loyalty program and attend an Infinity Vision showing of Avengers: Doomsday between December 17 and December 20. d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.title: The Scramble for the Open Seas
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.author: Michael Albertus
d006da4fe3:22627d45ff3f3498.summary: Over the last half millennium, societies around the globe competed to divide up the world’s land. Nearly every square inch of soil outside Antarctica is now owned and tucked within national borders. But the oceans have largely been spared that fate. There were times throughout history when countries tried to gate and regulate the seas, but they were too vast to be controlled for long periods. During the Cold War, as technology made it far easier to imagine partitioning the world’s waterways and seabeds, great powers avoided an unrestrained race to grab the oceans. Most governments agreed to deal with them through a patchwork of treaties and multilateral bodies that sought to guarantee freedom of navigation in international waters and assign coastal seabeds to adjacent littoral states.

d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.title: The Trouble With the Nuclear-AI Analogy
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.author: Christopher LaRoche, Ankit Panda
d006da4fe3:a574167532370f34.summary: In humanity’s quest to constrain the dangers from fast-advancing artificial intelligence, many have looked to the most revolutionary technology that preceded it: nuclear weapons. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk has called artificial intelligence “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who assigns The Making of the Atomic Bomb to employees and has likened himself to the Manhattan Project scientist Leo Szilard, describes the most powerful AI models as “weaponizable nuclear materials.” When asked how a technology such as AI can be regulated, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman often references the world’s nuclear materials watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency. Even the director of the CIA, John Ratcliffe, has made the same comparison.These comparisons capture real parallels. Like nuclear weapons, frontier AI is powerful and hard to control. Like nuclear technology, it can be used for good or for ill. And like the Cold War arms race, the race for AI breakthroughs may reorder the global balance of power. The nuclear analogy, then, seems to offer a blueprint for how to effectively govern a promising but potentially dangerous technology such as AI.

fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.title: Relative Development and the Intelligence Divide: Human Capital, Technology Diffusion, and AI
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.author: Jonathan R. W. Temple
fc066e842d:49934de94c848c00.summary: Will artificial intelligence (AI) help poorer countries catch up? This paper argues that the answer depends less on access to AI than on the capacity to use new knowledge productively. We show that countries have narrowed gaps in capital and schooling more readily than gaps in productivity. Technology can diffuse widely without producing productivity convergence. Measured human capital explains only a modest share of productivity differences in levels, but is associated with sharply different mobility regimes. The estimated transition processes imply an expected time to exit the lowest-productivity state of about 65 years for economies below the estimated human-capital threshold, compared with about 25 years for those above it. This reconciles development accounting with the view of human capital as absorptive capacity. If AI mainly augments skilled workers and capable firms, it may reinforce existing gaps. If it lowers the costs of learning, adaptation, and implementation in weaker-capability economies, it could instead promote convergence. The Intelligence Divide is therefore not simply about access to AI, but about the capacity to turn knowledge into productivity.

fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.title: Growth in Chains: EU Value Chain Productivity and its Slowdown
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.author: Lähdemäki, Sakari
fc066e842d:e0411ad22edea77d.summary: Abstract We study Europe’s post-2008 productivity slowdown using novel total factor productivity (TFP) measures that follow production beyond individual industries in global value chains (GVCs). We collect a newset of stylized facts: (1) the slowdown is broad-based, with productivity growth weakening both in final-producer industries and in upstream industries; (2) the staggered entry into force of bilateral investment treaties with China is followed by higher value-chain TFP and greater business-intangible investment; while (3) the gains associated with technology intangibles are weak. We use these facts to discipline a stylized two-region general-equilibrium model with business capabilities, technology-related knowledge, and cross-border knowledge spillovers. The calibration supports a two-stage interpretation of Europe’s experience: (1) sizeable initial integration gains because accumulated business capabilities convert market access into productivity, and (2) later losses when technology improvements are converted into productivity more effectively elsewhere.

fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.title: A Fork in the Road for Global AI Governance: To Repair or Reconfigure Expert-Led Governance?
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.author: Olugbade, Olajide
fc066e842d:1aed792933eb29e0.summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) has become a live object of global governance, with expert-led institutional arrangements emerging across an international regime complex. While scholarship on epistemic communities and science-policy interfaces treats expertise as a mechanism for coordination under uncertainty, recent work in Objectual International Relations (O-IR) and Science and Technology Studies foregrounds knowledge politics, contested authority, and the co-productive character of governance. We bring these perspectives into conversation with AI governance through a reflexive workshop design using Nominal Group Technique, drawing on two expert workshops in the UK and US. Findings show that expert panels remain valued for structuring debate, coordinating knowledge, and lending legitimacy to policy action. Yet participants identified tensions around exclusion, elite and private capture, weak accountability, geopolitical constraints, and temporal misalignment between institutional processes and technological change. An object-centered analysis further shows that AI remains an unstable governance object; the knowledge required to govern it is contested and unevenly distributed; and expertise itself is politically charged and institutionally unsettled. We synthesize these tensions into two pathways: Repair and Reconfiguration. Repair seeks to stabilize AI as a governable object, standardize relevant knowledge, and secure expert authority through institutional continuity and procedural refinement. Reconfiguration seeks to keep AI contested, broaden credible forms of knowledge, and reshape expertise through participation, reflexivity, and engagement with politics. The framework provides a critical lens for assessing emerging institutional designs for global AI governance and the trade-offs they entail.

fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.title: What Does Venture Capital Actually Finance ? Scale and Structure around the World
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.author: Mauro, Paolo
fc066e842d:b24979dbe73586d0.summary: Venture capital is widely viewed as financing knowledge-intensive, R&D-driven startups, but owing to data constraints, this view has been based largely on high-income economies. By taking a global perspective, this paper documents that what venture capital finances differs systematically across economies, varying with institutional and business conditions rather than following a single model. Using a new cross-country dataset that harmonizes firm-level venture capital records with equity issuance data for more than 150 economies, the data shows that VC markets differ across countries not only in scale but in kind. Outside high-income countries, rather than being concentrated in knowledge intangibles, venture capital tilts–at both the sector and firm levels–toward organizational intangibles such as distribution, logistics, and payments. Highlighting the unique features of venture capital, this pattern is absent from public equity markets, where sectoral composition is far more similar across income levels. An accounting decomposition separates venture capital depth into the rate at which firms enter the market and the funding each entrant attracts, and entry accounts for the largest cross-country gaps. Moreover, the business environment is associated with VC primarily through entry, linked both to the size of the market and to the composition of what venture capital finances, the latter through entry into knowledge-intensive sectors in particular.

fc066e842d:81f95d80d259f0cf.title: Black Feminist Social Work: Centering Black Women's Knowledge in Social Work Theory, Education, Research, Policy, and Practice
fc066e842d:81f95d80d259f0cf.author: Talley, Vanessa M.
fc066e842d:81f95d80d259f0cf.summary: Social work acknowledges Black Feminist Thought as a framework and praxis, yet the profession has not established a social work framework that explicitly centers Black women’s epistemologies as foundational to education, theory, research, policy, and practice. Although social work maintains a historical commitment to social justice, person-in-environment, and human rights perspectives, dominant theories and knowledge systems continue to reflect Eurocentric assumptions regarding knowledge production and professional expertise. This article introduces Black Feminist Social Work (BFSW) as a conceptual framework that centers Black women’s individual and collective lived experiences, intellectual traditions, historical resistance, and knowledge to inform social work theory, education, research, policy, and practice. Drawing upon Black feminism, Black Feminist Thought, Womanism, Intersectionality, and the profession’s ethical commitments, the BFSW framework proposes a necessary shift from positioning Black women primarily as a population to be studied to recognizing them as producers of transformative knowledge. This article introduces four organizing principles, the Four C’s: Centering, Contextualizing, Co-Creating, and Changing, as foundational processes for Black Feminist Social Work and discusses the implications for curriculum development, clinical practice, research methodologies, policy advocacy, and future scholarship. Rather than positioning Black Feminist Social Work as an alternative specialization, this framework argues that centering Black women’s knowledge expands the social work profession’s capacity to pursue equity, liberation, and social transformation.
